F o r e w o r d
The 7th Panchayat General Elections, 2008 for electing the members of the 3
tier Panchayati Raj System of West Bengal is just round the corner. Though being
associated with the conduction of Panchayat Elections is altogether a unique
experience, being completely different from the Parliamentary and Assembly
Elections, yet, this year’s Panchayat Elections is specially different leaving very
little time for preparations at various levels of administration, our district being in
phase I of the programme. There has been some modification in the instructions
issued by the State Election Commission since the last election in 2003 which has
necessitated many changes in our arrangements for the conduct of polls.
Holding of a smooth Panchayat Election requires a distinctly different
outlook & attitude, preparation and methodology as well as strategy and planning.
There are thousands of constituencies, seats and also a large no candidates who are
into fray. Votes for three tiers are to be caste at 3923 Polling Stations including 751
Auxiliary Polling Stations Preparatory works at various steps require to be
considerably decentralized and bringing about an adequate level of uniformity and
standardization is thus correspondingly difficult, particularly in a large district like
Burdwan.
However, the District Administration has pulled out all stops to ensure that
the arrangements are made full proof. This has been done through meticulous
planning, regular monitoring and above all co-operation and sincere participation of
all concerned. This handbook is being brought out to highlight some of the
arrangements made for the ensuing election. We hope that a booklet of such nature
will be put to use by all the election officials involved at various level and also by
the election observers appointed by the State Election Commission helping us in
better monitoring and supervision. I would like to place on record my sincere
appreciation to Dr. Archana, IAS, ADM (Election), Sri Hindole Dutta, DPRDO,
Burdwan, Smt. Sonali Dutta (Ray), W.B.C.S. (Exe), Smt. Soma Shaw W.B.C.S.
(Exe) and other members of staff, who worked relentlessly to bring out this booklet
in time.
I am confident that the Panchayat General Election 2008 will be conducted
in this district with distinction, fairness and efficiency owing to the competence,
dedication, sincerity and, above all, the team spirit of all the officers, staff members,
polling personnel, security personnel and all others involved in the election process. I
thank each and everyone of the team and convey my best wishes for smooth
conduction of the forthcoming election.
(Manish Jain)
Burdwan
District Panchayat Election Officer
The 6th of April, 2008
&
District Magistrate,Burdwan

The district of Burdwan is spread in East – West direction. The western
part of the district is industrialised while the eastern side is mainly dependent
on agriculture.
The district of Burdwan is spread over about 7024 sq. km. with a
population of about 69 lakh (2001 census). The district is divided into 6 sub-
divisions. These sub-divisions are comprised of 31 Development Blocks (i.e.
31 Panchayat Samities), 9 Municipalities and 2 Municipal Corporations. The
CD Blocks are further sub-divided into 277 Gram Panchayats. There are 26
Assembly Segments in this district. These 26 Assembly constituencies are
within 6 Parliamentary Constituencies some of which have assembly segments
in the neighbouring districts of Hooghly, Bankura, Birbhum and Murshidabad.

ELECTION PROFILE
To conduct free and fair poll impartially it is very important to chalk out every step
of the election process very meticulously and to verify it with the check list as
often as possible. It includes:
? Adherence to the fixture of election as laid down by the State Election
Commission.
? To review the previous election results so as to have an idea of trends of
voters, sensitivity etc.
? To know the accurate number of voters and distribution position of EPIC.
? Number of polling booths including auxilliary booths and premises. To
check the condition of booths and approach roads through physical
verification and to take up the minor repair works as and when necessary.
? Preparing the polling personnel through exhaustive training.
? Assessment of requirement and stock position of polling material and
procurement as per need.
? Selection of DC&RC and Counting Venues and erection of temporary
structure as per necessity.
? Ensuring full proof communication strategy through establishment of
required no. of sector offices in consultation with police and identification
of booth specific telephone nos. as far as practicable.
? Chalking out the proper mode of transmission (through installation of ear-
marked telephone, fax, e-network, etc.) for sharing of various
reports/returns in connection with Panchayat General Election maintaining
specific time schedule.
